title: Life Cycles
seo_title: Year 3 Science: Life Cycles Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Compare characteristics of living and non-living things and examine the differences between the life cycles of plants and animals (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 3 science worksheets on life cycles of plants and animals: frogs, butterflies, beetles, gum trees and Australian animals such as the platypus, kangaroo, emu and sea turtle. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Living things are born, grow, reproduce and die.
key_sub: Every plant and animal has a life cycle that starts again when it has young.
body_html:
How to think about it

A life cycle is the set of stages a living thing goes through as it grows and has young.

  • Many animals hatch from eggs; the platypus and echidna are mammals that lay eggs.
  • Kangaroos are born tiny and grow in their mother's pouch. Insects such as butterflies change shape: egg, larva, pupa, adult.
  • Plants grow from seeds into seedlings and adult plants that make flowers and new seeds.
Example

Frog: egg → tadpole → ? → adult frog

the tadpole grows legs and loses its tail

Answer: froglet

Example

Does a platypus lay eggs?

it is a monotreme

Answer: yes

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all mammals give birth to live young (the platypus and echidna lay eggs).
  • Mixing up the larva (caterpillar) and the pupa.
  • Thinking young animals always look like their parents.

faq.a: A life cycle is the series of stages a living thing goes through: for example egg, tadpole, froglet and adult frog.

faq.q: How is a kangaroo's life cycle different?
faq.a: A kangaroo is born very small, about the size of a jellybean. It crawls into its mother's pouch, drinks milk and grows there for months.
It is a big change in body shape during a life cycle, such as a caterpillar changing into a butterfly or a tadpole into a frog.

items.q: What happens inside a pupa?
c: The larva changes into an adult insect.
items.e: This change is called metamorphosis.

items.q: In the life cycle of a red kangaroo, what comes after the joey in the pouch?
c: young kangaroo out of the pouch
items.e: tiny newborn joey → joey in the pouch → young kangaroo out of the pouch → adult kangaroo.

items.q: In the life cycle of a Ulysses butterfly, what comes after the egg?
items.e: egg → caterpillar (larva) → pupa → adult butterfly.

items.q: What is metamorphosis?
c: a big change in body shape during a life cycle
items.e: Butterflies and frogs go through metamorphosis.

items.q: Which stage is missing from this life cycle of a red kangaroo? tiny newborn joey → ? → young kangaroo out of the pouch → adult kangaroo
c: young kangaroo out of the pouch
items.e: The full cycle: tiny newborn joey → joey in the pouch → young kangaroo out of the pouch → adult kangaroo.

items.q: A caterpillar is
c: a kind of worm that never changes
items.e: The caterpillar will become a pupa and then a butterfly.

items.q: In the life cycle of a red kangaroo, what comes after the young kangaroo out of the pouch?
c: young kangaroo out of the pouch
items.e: tiny newborn joey → joey in the pouch → young kangaroo out of the pouch → adult kangaroo.

items.q: What do the life cycles of a frog and a chicken have in common?
c: Both are born, grow, reproduce and die.
Neither one changes as it grows.
items.e: All living things are born, grow, reproduce and die.

items.q: What is the first stage in the life cycle of a platypus?
items.e: The cycle starts with egg.

items.q: How are the life cycles of a dog and a frog different?
c: A puppy looks like a small dog, but a tadpole looks very different from an adult frog.
A frog has no young stage.
items.e: A puppy looks like a small dog, but a tadpole looks very different from an adult frog.

items.q: What do the life cycles of a bean plant and a butterfly have in common?
c: Neither one changes as it grows.
Both are born, grow, reproduce and die.
items.e: All living things are born, grow, reproduce and die.

items.q: What is a life cycle?
c: the stages a living thing goes through from birth to having young of its own
items.e: Life cycles repeat.

items.q: Which parent sits on emu eggs until they hatch?
items.e: Emu fathers also care for the chicks.

items.q: What does a chrysalis (pupa) do?
c: protects the insect while its body changes into an adult
items.e: Inside, the caterpillar becomes a butterfly.

items.q: How are the life cycles of a ladybird and a dragonfly different?
c: The ladybird has a pupa stage; the dragonfly goes from nymph straight to adult.
The dragonfly has a pupa stage.
items.e: The ladybird has a pupa stage; the dragonfly goes from nymph straight to adult.

items.q: Why is a life cycle drawn as a circle?
c: The adults make new young, so the cycle starts again.
Because circles are easy to draw.
items.e: It keeps repeating.

items.q: A tadpole is
items.e: Tadpoles live in water and breathe with gills.

items.q: Which stage is missing from this life cycle of a green tree frog? egg → ? → froglet → adult frog
items.e: The full cycle: egg → tadpole → froglet → adult frog.

items.q: Which stage of a frog's life cycle lives only in water and breathes with gills?
items.e: Tadpoles change into frogs.

items.q: How are the life cycles of a frog and a chicken different?
c: A frog has a tadpole stage in water; a chicken hatches as a chick that looks like a small adult.
items.e: A frog has a tadpole stage in water; a chicken hatches as a chick that looks like a small adult.

items.q: What is the first stage in the life cycle of a red kangaroo?
c: young kangaroo out of the pouch
items.e: The cycle starts with tiny newborn joey.

items.q: In the life cycle of a sea turtle, which stage comes right after the egg?
items.e: The sea turtle life cycle: egg → hatchling → young turtle → adult turtle.

items.q: In the life cycle of a dragonfly, which stage comes right after the egg?
items.e: The dragonfly life cycle: egg → nymph → adult dragonfly.

items.q: What is the first stage in the life cycle of a Christmas beetle?
items.e: The cycle starts with egg.

items.q: In the life cycle of a gum tree, what comes after the young tree?
items.e: seed → seedling → young tree → adult tree with flowers.

items.q: In the life cycle of a Ulysses butterfly, what comes after the pupa?
items.e: egg → caterpillar (larva) → pupa → adult butterfly.

items.q: Which young animal does NOT look like its parent?
items.e: Caterpillars change a lot as they grow.

items.q: In the life cycle of a green tree frog, which stage can reproduce?
items.e: Only the adult can reproduce.

items.q: In the life cycle of a frog, which stage comes right after the froglet?
items.e: The frog life cycle: egg → tadpole → froglet → adult frog.

items.q: What is the first stage in the life cycle of a gum tree?
items.e: The cycle starts with seed.

items.q: What is the first stage in the life cycle of a green tree frog?
items.e: The cycle starts with egg.

items.q: Where does a newborn kangaroo joey grow?
items.e: Kangaroos are marsupials.

items.q: In the life cycle of a platypus, what comes after the puggle?
items.e: egg → puggle (baby platypus) → young platypus → adult platypus.

items.q: In the life cycle of an emu, which stage can reproduce?
items.e: Only the adult can reproduce.

items.q: In the life cycle of a red kangaroo, which stage can reproduce?
c: young kangaroo out of the pouch
items.e: Only the adult can reproduce.

items.q: Where do green sea turtles lay their eggs?
c: in holes they dig in sandy beaches
items.e: The hatchlings crawl to the sea.

items.q: In the life cycle of a red kangaroo, what comes after the tiny newborn joey?
c: young kangaroo out of the pouch
items.e: tiny newborn joey → joey in the pouch → young kangaroo out of the pouch → adult kangaroo.

items.q: In the life cycle of a platypus, which stage can reproduce?
items.e: Only the adult can reproduce.

items.q: In the life cycle of a green tree frog, what comes after the froglet?
items.e: egg → tadpole → froglet → adult frog.

items.q: Which Australian mammals lay eggs?
items.e: They are called monotremes.

items.q: Why does a nymph shed its skin (moult) several times?
c: Its hard outer skin does not grow, so it sheds it to grow bigger.
It is turning into a pupa.
items.e: Cockroach and grasshopper nymphs moult as they grow.

items.q: Which stage of a mosquito can fly?
items.e: Only adult mosquitoes have wings.

items.q: Which shows the life cycle of a butterfly in the correct order?
items.e: Start with the egg and end with the adult.

items.q: Where does a hen keep her eggs warm?
c: in a nest, by sitting on them
items.e: The heat helps the chicks develop.

items.q: This is the life cycle of a dog. Which stage is missing?
items.e: The dog life cycle: puppy → young dog → adult dog.

items.q: Where do tadpoles live?
items.e: Tadpoles breathe through gills.

items.q: Which shows the life cycle of a frog in the correct order?
c: adult frog → young frog → tadpole → egg
egg → tadpole → young frog → adult frog
tadpole → egg → young frog → adult frog
egg → young frog → tadpole → adult frog
items.e: Start with the egg and end with the adult.

items.q: What is a young frog that lives in water called?
items.e: Tadpoles have tails and gills.

items.q: Which shows the life cycle of a mosquito in the correct order?
items.e: Start with the egg and end with the adult.

items.q: Which shows the life cycle of a mealworm beetle in the correct order?
items.e: Start with the egg and end with the adult.

items.q: Which animal has a three-stage life cycle?
items.e: Egg → nymph → adult.

items.q: Which statement about a frog's life cycle is correct?
c: Tadpoles live in water; adult frogs can live on land and in water.
Frogs give birth to young frogs.
Adult frogs breathe only through gills.
items.e: Frogs are amphibians.

items.q: This is the life cycle of a dragonfly. Which stage is missing?
items.e: The dragonfly life cycle: egg → nymph → adult dragonfly.

items.q: Where do mosquito larvae live?
items.e: They hang below the water surface to breathe.

items.q: How is a nymph different from an adult grasshopper?
c: It is smaller and has no fully grown wings.
items.e: A nymph looks like a small adult.

items.q: What is the stage of a butterfly between the caterpillar and the adult?
items.e: Inside the pupa, the caterpillar changes into a butterfly.

items.q: This is the life cycle of a sea turtle. Which stage is missing?
items.e: The sea turtle life cycle: egg → hatchling → young turtle → adult turtle.

items.q: Where does a mosquito lay its eggs?
c: on the surface of still water
items.e: Mosquito larvae and pupae live in water.

items.q: Which stage comes first in the life cycle of most animals?
items.e: Many animals start life as an egg.

items.q: Which animal has a four-stage life cycle?
items.e: Egg → larva → pupa → adult.

items.q: What does the young root of a seed do?
c: It grows downwards and takes in water.
It protects the inside of the seed.
It stores food for the young plant.
It grows upwards towards the light.
items.e: Each part of the seed has a job.

items.q: In the life cycle of a flowering plant, what comes after the seed?
items.e: seed → germinating seed → seedling → young plant → adult plant with flowers → fruits with seeds.

items.q: Which part of a germinating seed grows upwards towards the light?
items.e: Each part of the seed has a job.

items.q: Which stage of a flowering plant can make seeds?
items.e: Only the adult plant makes flowers and fruits.

items.q: In the life cycle of a flowering plant, what comes just before the germinating seed?
items.e: seed → germinating seed → seedling → young plant → adult plant with flowers → fruits with seeds.

items.q: In the life cycle of a flowering plant, what comes just before the adult plant with flowers?
items.e: seed → germinating seed → seedling → young plant → adult plant with flowers → fruits with seeds.

items.q: In the life cycle of a flowering plant, what comes just before the young plant?
items.e: seed → germinating seed → seedling → young plant → adult plant with flowers → fruits with seeds.

items.q: What do the fruits of a plant do in the life cycle?
c: They protect the seeds and help spread them.
They take in water from the soil.
items.e: The seeds inside grow into new plants.

items.q: In the life cycle of a flowering plant, what comes just before the fruits with seeds?
items.e: seed → germinating seed → seedling → young plant → adult plant with flowers → fruits with seeds.

items.q: A green bean plant takes about 2 months to grow from a seed to a plant that makes seeds. A balsam plant takes about 3 months. Which has the longer life cycle?
items.e: Different plants take different lengths of time to complete their life cycles.

items.q: Where do the seeds of a flowering plant develop?
items.e: A papaya fruit contains many seeds.

items.q: What does the seed coat of a seed do?
c: It protects the inside of the seed.
It grows upwards towards the light.
It stores food for the young plant.
It grows downwards and takes in water.
items.e: Each part of the seed has a job.

items.q: A balsam plant takes about 3 months to grow from a seed to a plant that makes seeds. A mango tree takes about 5 years. Which has the longer life cycle?
items.e: Different plants take different lengths of time to complete their life cycles.

items.q: In the life cycle of a flowering plant, what comes just before the seedling?
items.e: seed → germinating seed → seedling → young plant → adult plant with flowers → fruits with seeds.

items.q: Which part of a germinating seed protects the inside of the seed?
items.e: Each part of the seed has a job.

items.q: Where does a germinating seed get its food before it has green leaves?
c: from the food stored in its seed leaves
items.e: That is why seeds can germinate without soil.

items.q: What does a seed need to germinate?
items.e: Seeds do not need light or soil to germinate.

items.q: What does the seed leaf of a seed do?
c: It protects the inside of the seed.
It grows downwards and takes in water.
It stores food for the young plant.
It grows upwards towards the light.
items.e: Each part of the seed has a job.

items.q: What is a seedling?
c: a seed that has not germinated
a young plant that has just grown from a seed
items.e: A seedling has its first leaves.

items.q: A rice plant takes about 4 months to grow from a seed to a plant that makes seeds. A mango tree takes about 5 years. Which has the longer life cycle?
items.e: Different plants take different lengths of time to complete their life cycles.

items.q: A student changes the water in his vase every 3 days. A mosquito egg takes 2 days to hatch and the larva takes 7 days to become a pupa. Can adult mosquitoes come from the vase?
c: No. The larvae are thrown away before they can become pupae.
No, because mosquitoes do not lay eggs in water.
Yes, because larvae can fly away.
Yes, the eggs hatch into adults straight away.
items.e: Changing the water often breaks the life cycle.

items.q: Kai plants bean seeds and records the plant every day. What should he expect to see first?
items.e: The seed grows into a seedling first.

items.q: Why do some animals lay many eggs?
c: Many eggs and young are eaten or die, so laying many helps some survive.
items.e: Frogs and fish lay hundreds of eggs.

items.q: Why do frogs lay so many eggs?
c: Many eggs and tadpoles are eaten, so laying many helps some survive.
Each egg grows into many frogs.
items.e: Only some young survive to become adults.

items.q: Noah wants to test whether seeds need water to germinate. Which pair of set-ups should he use?
c: wet cotton wool in a fridge and dry cotton wool in a room
wet cotton wool and dry cotton wool, both in the same warm room
wet cotton wool in the light and in the dark
items.e: Change only the water.

items.q: Mealworms are fed to pet birds. Which stage of the beetle is a mealworm?
items.e: A mealworm is the larva of the mealworm beetle.

items.q: Which observation shows that a butterfly's life cycle is complete?
c: The pupa hangs from a twig.
items.e: Laying eggs starts the cycle again.

items.q:
The table shows the life cycle of a mealworm beetle.
StageAbout how many days
egg10
larva (mealworm)60
pupa14
adult beetle60
At which stage does the animal eat the most and grow fastest?
items.e: The larva eats a lot. The pupa does not eat.

items.q: Priya kept mealworms in a container with oats. After three weeks, some stopped moving and turned pale and still. What stage were they?
items.e: The mealworm (larva) becomes a pupa before the adult beetle.

items.q: Mia measures a bean plant every 2 days: 0, 2, 5, 9, 14 cm. What pattern does she see?
c: It grows the same amount each time.
items.e: The gaps get bigger: 2, 3, 4, 5 cm.

items.q: Noah makes a model of a life cycle as a circle with arrows. Why is it a circle?
c: The adults make new young, so the cycle starts again.
Life cycles never end for one animal.
items.e: Reproduction starts the cycle again.

items.q: Jack keeps silkworms. He sees eggs, then caterpillars, then cocoons. What should he expect next?
items.e: Silkworms become moths.

items.q:
The table shows the life cycle of a mosquito.
StageAbout how many days
egg2
larva7
pupa2
adult mosquito14
At which stage does the animal eat the most and grow fastest?
items.e: The larva eats a lot. The pupa does not eat.

items.q: Why should we remove stagnant water from flower pot plates?
c: It makes the plants grow too fast.
Mosquitoes lay their eggs in still water.
items.e: No still water means no place for mosquito larvae to grow.

items.q: A student measured the height of two seedlings: one by the window and one in a dark cupboard. Which variable did she change?
items.e: Only the place (light) was different.

items.q: Ruby compares life cycle lengths: a mosquito about 2 weeks, a frog about 3 months to adult, a kangaroo about 2 years. Which takes longest to become an adult?
items.e: Bigger animals often take longer.

items.q:
The table shows the life cycle of a butterfly.
StageAbout how many days
egg4
caterpillar (larva)14
pupa10
adult butterfly14
About how many days does it take from egg to adult?
items.e: Add the days of the stages before the adult: 4 + 14 + 10 = 28.

items.q: Matilda put bean seeds on wet cotton wool in two dishes. Dish A was in the classroom; dish B was in a fridge. Only the seeds in A germinated. What was she testing?
c: whether seeds need warmth to germinate
items.e: Only the temperature was different.

items.q: A student kept a caterpillar in a container with fresh leaves. Why did she add fresh leaves every day?
c: The leaves keep the container dry.
The pupa needs leaves to eat.
Butterflies lay eggs only on dry leaves.
Caterpillars need a lot of food to grow.
items.e: The larva stage eats the most.

items.q: Why do students use more than one seed in each set-up?
c: So that they need less water.
Some seeds may not germinate, so using many gives a reliable result.
items.e: One seed might be dead.
